comment: Agent NDA identity, offer bytes, digests and signature bytes (agentnda.net 0.2.0-draft, 4.1, 6, 6.1, 8). Harbor & Line Outfitters signs an open offer to gate its freight-audit posting; Caldera Freight Systems accepts it. Pins the bytes where two implementations drift: the identifier hashes the version-1 offer minus id and signatures, with no prefix; the signed bytes are 'agent-nda-v1', one newline, then the JCS of the document minus signatures (id included); the offer bytes are re-derived from the completed document by setting parties.recipient and disclosure.recipient back to null; the offer digest and the agreement digest are 'sha256:' and 64 lowercase hex over those bytes. Each signature signs its own record: 'agent-nda-sig-v1', one newline, then the JCS of the record minus sig, where the record's digest names the bytes it covers (the offer digest for the discloser's record, marked over: offer, and the agreement digest for the recipient's). The agent keys in the seats are stand-ins in the family's key spelling, because the identifier and digests hash them; the language hash is the hash of a stand-in template. Owner keys are Ed25519 keys derived from published test seeds (nda-lifecycle.json, keys), each sig is the padded base64 of the 64-byte signature, and Ed25519 is deterministic, so any implementation reproduces them. Harbor & Line's seat names an organization, so it carries no owner_key and its signer is the holder.key of the mandate its record cites; Caldera's seat carries owner_key, which is why the agreement digest changed in 0.2.0-draft while the identifier and the offer digest did not. THE FIXTURE IS THE AUTHORITY: change it only with a spec change alongside.
spec: Agent NDA 0.2.0-draft: 4.1 (identity), 5.1 (owner_key), 6 (signed bytes and signature bytes), 6.1 (open offers), 8 (references)

traps.why: the id hashes the bytes minus id AND signatures, without the prefix; hashing the signed bytes gives a different id
digests are over the signed bytes, which exclude signatures; adding a signature never changes a digest
an Agent SoW names the agreement digest (recipient filled); the offer digest is what a gated posting names
digests are lowercase hex and compared exactly
any change beyond parties.recipient and disclosure.recipient makes the re-derived offer bytes differ, and the discloser's signature fails
each signature signs its own record with sig removed, so changing signed_at, mandate, key, over or agent breaks it; before 0.2.0-draft the record sat outside every signed byte string
a record's digest must equal the digest of the bytes it covers; a record that verifies over another document's digest does not cover this one
a valid signature by a key that is not the seat's owner_key, or for an organization seat the cited mandate's holder.key, does not count for the seat

sig is the canonical padded base64 of 64 bytes: 86 characters from the standard alphabet and '==', with the unused bits of the last character zero; base64url, missing padding or other trailing bits are refused
